about.text: A pressed raw-milk cow's cheese from Serra da Canastra in south-west Minas Gerais, Brazil, sold fresh (about 4 days), half-cured or fully cured (about 40 days). Part of the Minas artisanal cheese craft that IPHAN recognised as national heritage in 2008.

how.label: add pingo, press by hand
how.text: Raw cow's milk is set with commercial rennet and the pingo, the drained whey of yesterday's cheeses, which carries the dairy's own lactic flora from batch to batch. The curd is pressed in the mould and the cheese is turned, salted and ripened for a few days to weeks.

steps.note: With coalho and the pingo, the previous day's drained whey.

processing.text: The pingo is whey drained from the previous day's cheeses. Some makers use rala, scraped from a 3-5 day old cheese. A survey of artisanal Minas cheeses found mostly Lactobacillus, with Lactococcus, Enterococcus and Weissella.

facts.v: In a survey of artisanal Minas cheeses from five regions (Serro, Canastra, Serra do Salitre, Araxa, Campo das Vertentes) lactic acid bacteria predominated, Lactobacillus most of all, with Lactococcus, Enterococcus and Weissella (Nero et al. 2017)
Some Serro makers use 'rala', scraped from a 3–5 day old cheese, instead of pingo
The Minas artisanal cheese 'modo de fazer' of Serro, Canastra and Serra do Salitre/Alto Paranaiba was recognised by IPHAN in 2008
